content: {"summary":"When a pod shows ~70% throttled periods but its average CPU usage stays low, first suspect CFS throttling rather than genuine load. Check the throttling ratio (above ~25% is a strong sign) and compare it to average CPU. Then examine the container’s thread count versus its CPU limit – a thread count sized to the node (e.g., GOMAXPROCS or WEB_CONCURRENCY set to node cores) is a common cause of excessive throttling. Verify by inspecting cgroup stats (nr_throttled/nr_periods or throttled_usec growth) and confirming the process’s configured thread/worker count matches the container limit.","likely_cause":"Thread‑count mismatch (process using more threads than the container CPU limit) leading to CFS throttling","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"High throttling with low average CPU suggests CFS throttling, not real load","evidence_ids":["RB-002#0","RB-002#1"],"quote":"If a service's p99 latency climbs while its CPU graph looks comfortable, suspect CFS throttling"},{"text":"Thread‑count sized to node instead of container limit commonly triggers throttling","evidence_ids":["RB-002#2"],"quote":"The usual trigger is a thread count sized to the node instead of the container."},{"text":"Verify mismatch by checking GOMAXPROCS/worker count and cgroup throttling stats","evidence_ids":["RB-002#2","RB-002#1"],"quote":"Run it twice a few seconds apart and look at how much `throttled_usec` grows."}],"next_checks":["Check the \"Container CPU\" panel for throttled periods ratio (>25% indicates throttling)","Run `kubectl exec <pod> -- cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat` twice and compare `nr_throttled`/`throttled_usec` growth","Inspect the pod’s GOMAXPROCS (Go) or WEB_CONCURRENCY (Python) to ensure it matches the CPU limit","List busy threads inside the pod (e.g., `top -H -p 1`) and verify the count does not exceed the container’s CPU limit"]}
